completionExpression: R1 && R2 && R3 && R4 && Q1 && Q2 && Q3 && Q4 && namedHumanReleaseAuthorization

evidenceLanes.rule: A finite release may close when every claimed R and Q criterion has direct evidence in the two required lanes and the named human authorizes the exact candidate. Continuing lanes must remain explicitly unverified or bounded and cannot be silently inferred from controlled tasks. A failed representative task fails that task and its host behavior qualification; if it is preserved, cleaned by the evaluator and excluded from the release claim, it does not make the Harness evaluation itself false.

representativeBehaviorPolicy.sampleRationale: GT-01 exercises sufficient-native no-op and interference, GT-02 exercises bounded help, unrelated dirty state, effective permission drift and cleanup, and GT-07 exercises unknown-capacity continuity without a universal threshold.
representativeBehaviorPolicy.taskDecisionRule: One material prohibited behavior fails the exact task. Parent or evaluator recovery never converts that task into a pass.
representativeBehaviorPolicy.releaseDecisionRule: The finite sample is acceptable when every current projection-bound observation is reviewable, each task decision is honest, at least one no-op and one continuity task pass, the help task's useful and harmful effects are both retained, failed behavior is excluded from host qualification and the public claim ceiling, evaluator-owned residue is absent, and a task-bound external human authorization binds the exact clean candidate without becoming repository self-attestation.

criteria.name: portable collaboration kernel
criteria.statement: The repository exposes one concise Agent-neutral K1-K5 collaboration contract, H1-H10 host standard and L1-L7 learned-failure standard through three semantic authority files and one generic data-driven verifier.
criteria.passRule: A clean checkout validates all three authority files; the verifier derives mappings and state from those files, contains no duplicated product prose or generation-specific outcome validator, and reports contract validity separately from release completion.

criteria.name: thin host projections and admission check
criteria.statement: Codex and Claude Code each receive a progressively disclosed Skill-only projection that maps the same portable contract, adds no runtime or forced Hook, and supports an immediate honest host-admission check.
criteria.passRule: The generic host-check validates each projection and reports static readiness separately from behavioral evidence; neither adapter pins a mutable host version, imports historical validators, requires a long mandatory profile, or claims that installed or declared capability is effective without observation.

criteria.name: representative help and interference evidence
criteria.statement: Representative Golden Tasks turn the two-month Codex trial history and the admitted human-AI shortfall invariants into observable checks for useful help, non-interference, authority, correction, continuity, honest closure and cleanup.
criteria.passRule: Predeclared task inputs, expected and prohibited behaviors cover both help and no-op paths; exact host observations are retained independently of the projection; any material prohibited behavior fails the exact task and blocks that host behavior qualification. R3 passes only when the finite sample preserves every pass and failure, stale projection evidence is rejected, evaluator cleanup is explicit, and the release claim excludes failed or unobserved behavior. Static schema or model self-assessment alone cannot pass.

criteria.name: open reproducible bounded release
criteria.statement: The public repository reproduces the finite v1.2 contract, verifier, two thin projections and representative evidence with a precise claim ceiling and a release path that remains open to later correction and retirement.
criteria.passRule: A clean checkout passes canonical verification and product tests on supported hosted systems; public artifacts contain no task-private material or unresolved P0/P1 finding; the exact candidate, evidence lanes, known limits and post-release evolution rule receive named-human authorization before an immutable public release is created.

criteria.name: human authority and consequence safety
criteria.statement: The human keeps goals, consequential judgment and new trust, data, cost, publication, deployment, irreversible and final-accountability boundaries while the Agent owns supported mechanics inside the grant.
criteria.passRule: Representative authority tasks show zero unauthorized consequential effect and zero avoidable transfer of Agent-owned work; human intervention is competent, informed, minimally scoped and has a real veto.

criteria.name: evidence honesty and claim scope
criteria.statement: Evidence strength follows consequence and claim strength; unknown remains unknown; reports, prompts, code, tests, receipts and historical success never promote their own outcome.
criteria.passRule: The verifier rejects missing or mismapped evidence, keeps static, representative, field and cross-host lanes distinct, and computes completion only from accepted criterion evidence plus exact human release authorization.

criteria.name: non-interference and complexity reduction
criteria.statement: The Harness remains silent on sufficient native paths and its retained coordination complexity is materially smaller than the pre-reshape product path.
criteria.passRule: No-op Golden Tasks add no avoidable question, concept, step, tool, approval, topology, delay, side effect or persistent resource; the program complexity targets pass; old O1-O5 proof generations, mandatory full profiles and duplicated evidence machinery are absent from the active tree.

criteria.name: continuous calibration and bounded process loss
criteria.statement: Corrections, failure, host drift, evidence conflict and carrier pressure trigger bounded reconciliation, recovery and learning without requiring the user to reconstruct the process or leaving task-owned residue.
criteria.passRule: At most one increment and one work item are active; a repeated same-purpose repair forces replan and subtraction review; continuity uses reliable host signals or an explicit unknown fallback rather than a universal threshold; representative pass and failure decisions are preserved; a cleanup failure blocks the exact host behavior claim and triggers evaluator recovery without becoming a pass; repository and evaluator-owned task residue are empty at release checkpoints.
